items.body: The fix depends on which it is.
The city's relief sewers added capacity. Your lateral and basement protection are still up to you.

bodies: Some water is a plumbing problem and some comes through the foundation. We handle the plumbing side: backflow valves, standpipes, [overhead sewer systems](/evanston/overhead-sewer-systems), [sump pumps](/evanston/sump-pumps) and battery backups.
If water is seeping through cracks in the walls, a waterproofing contractor is the right call, and we'll tell you so.

blocks.h2: Steps That Lower Your Flood Risk
blocks.body: Start with the cheap ones. Keep downspouts pointed away from the house. Clean catch basins and window wells every fall. Make sure the ground slopes away from the foundation. Then look at the plumbing: a clear lateral, a working sump pump with a backup and, if you've had sewer water in the basement, a backflow valve or overhead sewer. Together, these cover the most common ways water gets into an Evanston basement.

blocks.h2: Basement Flooding Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: How do I know if it's sewer water or groundwater?
items.answer: Through the floor drain is usually sewer water. Along the walls is usually groundwater.

items.preview: We fix the cause. A restoration company dries it.
items.answer: We fix the plumbing cause. A restoration company handles water removal and drying.

items.q: What's the best protection for an Evanston basement?
items.answer: For repeat sewer backups, an overhead sewer. For groundwater, a sump pump with a battery backup.

items.preview: Sewer backups often need a rider.
items.answer: Sewer backup usually needs a separate rider. Groundwater is often excluded. Check with your agent.

items.q: Should I finish my basement if it has flooded before?
items.answer: Fix the cause first. Then finish with materials that tolerate moisture.

items.q: How much does basement flooding repair cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the cause. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the cause and what's needed. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
